title: Chloroform Phenol Phage Genome Isolation
author: Marijn Ceelen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7kvhkw6

steps.title: Nuclease treatment of phage stock
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL 10× DNase I buffer, 1 µL DNase I (1 U/µL) and 1 µL RNase A (10 mg/mL) to the cleaned phage stock and incubate 1 h 30 min at 37 °C without shaking to degrade residual E. coli DNA and RNA.

steps.title: Inactivate nucleases with EDTA
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL 0.5 M EDTA (giving a final concentration of 20 M) and incubate 15 min at 75 °C to deactivate DNase I and RNase A.

steps.title: Proteinase K and SDS digestion
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL Proteinase K (20 mg/mL) and 50 µL 10 % SDS to the reaction, then incubate overnight (≈16 h) at 56 °C without shaking to digest the phage capsid.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform‑isoamyl extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1) to the lysate, mix gently (do not vortex), then centrifuge at room temperature for 10 min at 10 000 × g.

steps.title: Chloroform‑isoamyl wash
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (24:1), mix gently (do not vortex), and centrifuge at room temperature for 10 min at 10 000 × g.

steps.title: DNA precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 1/10 volume of 3 M sodium acetate, then add 2.5 volumes of 100 % ethanol, mix, incubate for 30 min (temperature not specified), and centrifuge 10 min at 4 668 × g.

steps.title: Pellet wash and drying
steps.instruction: Rinse the DNA pellet with 70 % ethanol, remove the supernatant, dry the pellet, and optionally heat at 50 °C to accelerate drying.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Dissolve the dried pellet in molecular‑grade (MQ) water.
